## Architecture Guidance Metadata

```yaml
guidance_id: 'GUID-<DOMAIN>-<CAP>-<TYPE>-SBB-4.D.NN'
guidance_name: '<Name>: Solution Building Block'
guidance_type: 'solution-building-block'
sbb_type: '<composite / component>'
realized_abb: '<GUID-<DOMAIN>-<CAP>-<TYPE>-2.D.NN>'       # Component ABB this SBB realizes
paired_rad: '<GUID-<DOMAIN>-<CAP>-<TYPE>-RAD-3.D.NN>'     # Reference Architecture this SBB implements
validates_bdd: '<GUID-<DOMAIN>-<CAP>-<TYPE>-BDD-3.5.D.NN>' # BDD Specification this SBB is evaluated against
parent_vision: '<GUID-<DOMAIN>-<CAP>-VISION-0.D.NN>'
adm_phase: 'Phase E-F'
category: '<application | business | infrastructure | information | technology | itsm-operations | governance>'
version: '0.1.0'
status: 'draft'
applicability: '<enterprise | domain | project | component>'
product_name: '<Vendor Product / Open Source Project Name>'
product_version: '<e.g., 2.x, 4.1.x — use the minimum supported version>'
tags: ['<domain>', '<capability-tag>', 'solution-building-block', 'phase-e', 'phase-f']
author: '<Author Name>'
```

> **Before authoring this SBB**: verify the Component ABB, Reference Architecture (RAD), AND BDD Specification all exist at `draft` status or higher. SBBs must not be authored before all three prerequisites exist. See `togaf-artifact-creation-guidelines.md` §2.0 in the same artifacts template directory — update this path when copying this template to its production location.

---

> **TOGAF ADM Note — Phase E–F (Opportunities & Solutions / Migration Planning)**: This document is a **Solution Building Block (SBB)**. SBBs are physical, product-specific implementations that realize the logical capabilities defined in a parent Architecture Building Block (ABB). Unlike ABBs — which are technology-agnostic — SBBs reference specific products, versions, configurations, and vendor capabilities.
>
> SBBs are authoritative inputs to project-level solution design, procurement decisions, and platform engineering runbooks. They SHALL NOT define new architectural requirements; all normative requirements are inherited from the parent ABB. SBBs are evaluated against the paired BDD Specification — every ABB SHALL requirement must be addressed in the Capability Delivery Matrix.

### Normative Language Inheritance

Per the parent ABB: **SHALL** = mandatory; **SHOULD** = strongly recommended; **MAY** = optional. This SBB adds no new normative requirements — it provides implementation-level detail for requirements established in the parent ABB.

## Capability Delivery Matrix

> This matrix is the core compliance section of every SBB. It maps every ABB SHALL and SHOULD requirement to the specific product capability, configuration, or feature that satisfies it. Every ABB SHALL must be addressed. Gaps must be explicitly documented.

| ABB Req ID | Requirement | Delivered By | Notes / Gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| `REQ-<DOMAIN>-<CAP>-001` | <Requirement text from ABB> | <Product feature or configuration that satisfies it> | ✓ Full coverage |
| `REQ-<DOMAIN>-<CAP>-002` | <Requirement text from ABB> | <Product feature or configuration> | ✓ Full coverage |
| `REQ-<DOMAIN>-<CAP>-003` | <Requirement text from ABB> | <Product feature or configuration> | ⚠ Partial — <describe gap and mitigation> |
| `REQ-<DOMAIN>-<CAP>-010` | <SHOULD requirement> | <Product feature, if implemented> | ⚠ Not natively supported — compensating control: <describe> |

**Coverage Summary:**

- SHALLs fully covered: `N / N`
- SHALLs partially covered: `N / N` *(document compensating controls)*
- SHALLs not covered: `N / N` *(document accepted risk or alternative SBB required)*
